import os, importlib.util, shutil

from pypdf import PdfReader

r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages:',len(r.pages))
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts)[:33000])

strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction offers an original, practical approximation to difficult three-view geometry problems using established 5-point/6-point and P3P solvers. The training-free mean-point variants are particularly useful as simple four-point baselines. This contribution provides the strongest reason for weak acceptance.

The real-data results demonstrate competitive four-point estimation. In Table 1, 4p3v(M±0.15) improves Sacre Coeur AUC@5° from 42.81 for the homotopy solver to 44.51, and reduces St. Peter’s Square median error from 9.73° to 8.92°. Table 2 also shows a useful accuracy/runtime tradeoff against 6pt+P3P on KITTI.

The evaluation includes 10,000 real image triplets, controlled noise and outlier experiments, shift ablations, and informative oracle comparisons. The supplementary geometric argument supports the centroid heuristic. The manuscript explicitly acknowledges approximation error and circumstances where sampling an additional real correspondence performs better.

The supplementary two-view experiment provides additional evidence of usefulness: Table 6 reports a runtime reduction from 0.04 s to 0.02 s, with AUC@5° decreasing from 63.71 to 61.80. This demonstrates a concrete accuracy/runtime tradeoff beyond the principal three-view application.
weaknesses: The claimed advantage under limited computation is only partially established. Figures 3 and 8–10 compare RANSAC iteration counts, although shifted variants invoke three minimal solves and learned variants cost 450–1130 microseconds per hypothesis-generation call versus 77.90 for 5pt+P3P. These plots establish sampling efficiency, but equal-time comparisons are needed to establish the claimed runtime advantage under heavy outlier contamination.

The unknown-shared-focal contribution is less thoroughly validated. Its real-data evaluation is restricted to KITTI stereo/adjacent-frame triplets, and neither the real nor synthetic experiments report focal-length accuracy. Good rotation and translation-direction estimates alone do not establish reliable focal recovery across general camera configurations.

The learned component adds limited demonstrated value relative to its overhead. On Sacre Coeur, the shifted learned variant improves AUC@5° only from 44.51 to 44.89 over the shifted mean baseline, while solver time increases from 218.71 to 511.28 microseconds. Improvements are inconsistent across scenes, and the partially calibrated variant reuses the calibrated network without demonstrating that this transfer is well suited to unknown focal lengths.

Equation (2), presented as the training loss, is a signed normalized epipolar residual rather than a nonnegative Sampson loss. Minimizing it literally need not move predictions toward the epipolar line. The missing absolute value or square is a mathematical specification defect; the manuscript does not resolve whether it also affects the implementation. This concern applies primarily to the learned branch.

Reproducibility of the complete estimator is weaker than that of the basic construction: RANSAC inlier thresholds, stopping criteria, and local refinement are insufficiently specified. Shift parameters are assessed on the same scenes used for the principal results, without a clearly separated selection protocol or reported run-to-run variability, making the smaller performance differences difficult to assess.
